question: Can the predecessor's GND-zone approach replace the clustered rooted-star GND copper while retaining only enough stitching vias for native connectivity?

method.via_selection: Retain the first existing GND via in each square cell anchored at the board minimum coordinate.
method.acceptance_authority: kicad-cli pcb drc --refill-zones with ERC, DRC, schematic parity, and selected-net connectivity

conclusion: The zone lifecycle is viable and removes the observed GND via clusters as routed meshes. The selected tested point removes every GND track and 75% of its vias while preserving native completeness. It is the sparsest passing member of this tested cell-size portfolio, not a proof of a global minimum.
limitations: Cell selection is deterministic but order-sensitive and uses the existing rooted-star vias as a seed pool.
Changing cell size changes which vias survive, so trial results are not a monotone via-count search.
The rectangular zones may contain isolated filled islands; KiCad connectivity, not polygon presence, determines success.
Foreign filled zones now yield during signal repair, but the router does not score lost plane area, narrow necks, or island quality.
This experiment measures validity and topology reduction, not plane impedance, thermal behavior, EMC, or runtime.
